hypotheses.reasoning: The first error on the ingest path is at 19:11:22: the third-party geo-IP provider (api.geoip.example) answered enrichment-svc with 503 Service Unavailable (#3460). It kept failing after that with 502s (#3575), 10s timeouts (#3522, #3611), and half-open probes that also got 503 or 502 (#3877, #4756). At 19:12:56 the circuit breaker opened at a 96% failure rate. From then on enrichment-svc returned 503 (circuit open) to ingest-api, ingest-api returned 503 to ingest-gateway, and that is the 503 rate on POST /v1/events that paged. The provider mostly sent back 5xx errors and the breaker probes kept failing, so this reads as the provider being down. The timeouts alone would point to dependency_timeout. I found no deploy and no internal fault that comes before 19:11:22.
Some geo-IP calls hung until the 10s timeout, and that slowness may have added to the failure rate that opened the breaker.

Starting at 19:16, accounts-db reports that column status_v2 is missing, which breaks /login through account-svc. This begins after the ingest failures and is on a different path, so it is a separate problem and not the cause of the /v1/events 503s. It still needs its own follow-up.

verdict.recommendedAction: Check the geo-IP provider's status and contact the vendor. While it's down, have enrichment-svc skip geo enrichment (fail open: accept events without geo data, or with cached geo data) so ingest-api stops returning 503s. Look at a backup provider. Separately, look into the missing accounts.status_v2 column that is breaking /login. That looks like a migration that wasn't fully applied, or code that went out before its migration ran.
